question: Identify the conjugate acid of HPO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup>.
explanation: Adding a proton to HPO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup> gives H<sub>2</sub>PO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup>.

question: Which of the following is a Lewis acid but does not fit the classical Brønsted-Lowry acid definition?
explanation: BF<sub>3</sub> accepts an electron pair but contains no hydrogen to donate as a proton.

question: What is the pH of a 0.01 M HCl solution assuming complete dissociation?
Which species acts as a Brønsted base in the reaction: CH<sub>3</sub>COOH + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇄ CH<sub>3</sub>COO<sup>-</sup> + H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>?
explanation: Water accepts a proton from acetic acid, acting as a Brønsted base.

question: Which of the following has the highest pK<sub>a</sub>?
explanation: Ammonia is a very weak acid (extremely reluctant to donate H<sup>+</sup>), corresponding to an extremely high pK<sub>a</sub>.

question: What is the value of pK<sub>w</sub> at 298 K?
Which ion undergoes cationic hydrolysis to produce an acidic aqueous solution?
explanation: NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> is the conjugate acid of a weak base (NH<sub>3</sub>) and hydrolyzes to produce H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup> ions.

question: What is the conjugate base of the ammonium ion (NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup>)?
explanation: Removing a proton from NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> yields ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>).

question: Which of the following represents an amphiprotic pair?
explanation: Water and hydroxide ions are part of acid-base conjugate systems, but H<sub>2</sub>O itself is amphiprotic (can act as acid or base).

question: In the reaction between HF and H<sub>2</sub>O, which species is the conjugate acid?
explanation: When water accepts a proton from HF, it forms the hydronium ion (H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>), which is the conjugate acid of H<sub>2</sub>O.
